sources_note: Dates and outcomes from SpaceX flight pages, Wikipedia List of Starship launches, NASASpaceflight, and FAA public mishap statements. Unknown where not published.

flights.booster_failure_stage: before planned splashdown — vehicle destroyed with stack at ~39 km
flights.ship_failure_stage: transatmospheric test — spin before staging; FTS
flights.engines_note: Several of 33 booster engines shut down before/during ascent; full staging not achieved
key_firsts: First integrated Starship + Super Heavy launch
flights.summary_line: Booster precluded; ship lost on ascent before staging (FTS).

flights.booster_failure_stage: after hot-staging — lost during boostback burn (~149 km stack)
flights.ship_failure_stage: ascent ~149 km — LOX vent fire; FTS
flights.engines_note: 33 engines to full duration on ascent; booster RUD after separation
flights.summary_line: Hot-staging OK; booster lost on boostback; ship lost on ascent (FTS).

flights.booster_failure_stage: Gulf landing burn — lost ~400 m above ocean
flights.engines_note: 13 of 33 relit boostback; 6 shut down early; 3 of 13 on landing burn
flights.payload_note: propellant transfer demo; Starlink door test
flights.summary_line: Ship reached high apogee; booster lost on landing burn; ship lost on reentry.

flights.ship_failure_stage: none — Indian Ocean splashdown (~6 km off target)
flights.engines_note: One Raptor lost early on ascent; ship six-engine landing burn succeeded
key_firsts: First controlled splashdown of both stages
flights.summary_line: First dual soft ocean landings; booster and ship controlled splashdowns.

flights.engines_note: Full duration; no engine loss entire flight
key_firsts: First Super Heavy catch by launch tower
flights.summary_line: First booster catch; ship soft splashdown Indian Ocean.

flights.booster_failure_stage: catch aborted — tower damage at liftoff; Gulf divert
flights.engines_note: In-space Raptor relight demonstrated on ship
key_firsts: In-space engine relight; last Block 1 ship
flights.summary_line: Booster catch aborted to Gulf; ship relight + controlled splashdown.

flights.ship_failure_stage: ascent — propellant leak; FTS ~3 min after telemetry loss
flights.engines_note: Ship engines shut down early; booster caught on OLP-1
key_firsts: First Block 2 ship; payload bay simulators
flights.summary_line: Booster caught; Block 2 ship lost on ascent (leak/FTS).

flights.booster_failure_stage: none — two boostback engines failed to relight initially
flights.ship_failure_stage: ascent — engine failures; loss of control
flights.engines_note: Ship multiple engine outs; booster catch despite boostback engine issues
flights.summary_line: Booster caught again; ship lost on ascent.

flights.booster_failure_stage: landing burn — RUD ~6 min (downcomer); hard splashdown test
flights.ship_failure_stage: reentry — attitude control loss after failed payload deploy
flights.engines_note: First booster reuse; SECO reached; 8 simulators not deployed
flights.faa_mishap: yes — ship mishap investigation (booster under test exception)
flights.summary_line: First booster reuse; both stages lost (hard splashdown / reentry).

flights.ship_failure_stage: none — heavy heat shield damage but soft splashdown
flights.engines_note: Booster lost one engine on ascent; ship in-space relight; 8 simulators deployed
key_firsts: Block 2 return to full mission success profile
flights.summary_line: Simulators deployed; controlled Gulf + Indian Ocean splashdowns.

flights.booster_failure_stage: none — Gulf; lost one engine on boostback, relit for landing
flights.engines_note: 24 engines reflown on booster; in-space relight on ship
key_firsts: Last Block 2 vehicles; last launch from OLP-1 before pad rebuild
flights.summary_line: Final Block 2 flight; dual controlled splashdowns.

flights.ship_failure_stage: none — one RV engine out on ascent
flights.engines_note: 20 of 33 boostback engines failed startup; ship SECO with engine-out
flights.summary_line: Block 3 debut; booster destroyed; ship controlled splashdown.

flights.ship_failure_stage: none — tipped after splashdown; survived for inspection
flights.engines_note: 10 of 13 landing engines lit then lost on booster
flights.payload_note: 20 Starlink V3 deployed (burned up after test)
key_firsts: First Starlink V3 deployment from Starship
flights.summary_line: Starlink V3 deploy; booster lost; ship soft splashdown survived tip-over.

flights.booster_failure_stage: none — Gulf; several engines out on descent
flights.ship_failure_stage: none — LEO ~275 km; 26 Starlink V3; Pacific splashdown
flights.engines_note: One ship engine out on ascent; orbital insertion proceeded
key_firsts: First orbital Starship mission; first operational payload to LEO
flights.summary_line: First orbital flight; 26 Starlink V3 deployed; booster Gulf splashdown; ship Pacific splashdown.

learnings: Booster tower catches worked on Flights 5, 7, and 8, but Flight 6 showed catch depends on tower health — aborts can divert to the Gulf instead.
Controlled ocean splashdowns for both stages (from Flight 4 onward) became the routine backup when a catch is not attempted.
Block 1 ships ended on Flight 6 after proving reentry and in-space relight; pad and hot-staging fixes followed Flights 1–2 FAA work.
Block 2 ships struggled in early 2025 (Flights 7–9) with ascent leaks and engine-outs; all three triggered FAA mishap reviews.
Block 2 recovered with Flights 10–11: simulators deployed, in-space relights, and soft ship splashdowns before retiring the version.
Block 3 moved launches to OLP-2; Flight 12–13 lost boosters on landing burns but ships completed payload and splashdown objectives.
Flight 14 reached Earth orbit and deployed operational Starlink — the milestone Block 2 had aimed for but not achieved.
Booster reuse began on Flight 9 (B14); landing-burn hardware remains the weak point when boosters are expended to test limits.
